aircrafts.description: The CoAX 600 is a two-seat coaxial ultralight helicopter with German type certification. Two counter-rotating rotor planes on one mast remove the need for a tail rotor, and the full 160 hp of its six-cylinder engine goes into lift. Available as a piloted UL helicopter, and as a compact VTOL base for optionally piloted or autonomous conversion.
details: No tail rotor: counter-rotating rotors cancel torque, which removes a major hazard on the ground and in flight.
600 kg MTOW, 340 kg empty weight, 150 km/h cruise, 12,000 ft ceiling and about 19 l/h fuel burn.

aircrafts.seoTitle: CoAX 600 Coaxial Ultralight Helicopter: Specs & Price
aircrafts.seoDescription: CoAX 600: two-seat coaxial UL helicopter with no tail rotor. 160 hp, 600 kg MTOW, 150 km/h cruise, German type certificate. Specs, autonomous conversion and enquiry.
aircrafts.summary: The CoAX 600 is a two-seat ultralight helicopter (UL class, 600 kg maximum take-off weight) with a coaxial main rotor: two counter-rotating rotor planes on a single mast. Because their torque cancels out, it needs no tail rotor. A 160 hp ULPower UL390iS six-cylinder engine drives it to a 150 km/h cruise and a 12,000 ft service ceiling on about 19 litres of fuel per hour. It holds a German type certificate (June 2023) and is offered both as a piloted helicopter and as a base airframe for optionally piloted or autonomous VTOL missions.

features.title: No tail rotor, fewer hazards
features.text: The two rotor planes turn in opposite directions, so their torque cancels out and no tail rotor is needed. That removes one of the most common causes of helicopter accidents and makes it safer to work around the aircraft on the ground.

features.title: All the power goes into lift
features.text: A conventional helicopter spends part of its engine power driving the tail rotor. In the CoAX 600 the full engine output turns the main rotor, which gives noticeably more lift for its weight class.

features.title: Teetering rotor, longer service life
features.text: Each rotor plane carries two blades on a central flapping hinge. This teetering layout keeps the centre of gravity steady while the blades turn and takes load off the blades and mast, so the structure lasts longer.

features.title: More energy for autorotation
features.text: With 2 × 2 blades, the rotor stores much more kinetic energy than a single two-blade rotor. If the engine stops, the pilot has more time and control for an autorotation landing.

features.title: Compact, VTOL-ready footprint
features.text: At 7.2 m long with a 6.5 m rotor and 1.65 m skid width, it fits small pads, trailers and ship decks. That compact size, plus about 260 kg of useful load, makes it a strong base for an optionally piloted or autonomous VTOL platform.

features.title: German type-certified
features.text: The CoAX 600 received its German UL-helicopter type certificate on 27 June 2023. Its predecessor was the first coaxial ultralight helicopter certified in Germany, in 2017.

mediaSections.title: Two rotor planes, one precision mast
paragraphs: The rotor mast is the heart of the CoAX 600. It carries both rotor planes and combines several aerospace materials under a hard-wearing protective coating. Each plane uses a teetering hub: two opposing blades on a central flapping hinge, a proven layout that keeps loads on the mast low.

The blades were developed for this aircraft and are made from fibre-composite materials. Each is 3,020 mm long with a 220 mm chord and 6.5° of twist, and runs at a tip speed of 155 m/s at 100 % rpm. The result is a long service life and consistent behaviour in flight.

images.alt: CoAX 600 coaxial rotor mast with upper and lower teetering hubs and control rods
Engineering drawing of the CoAX 600 coaxial rotor mast and gearbox
Set of four fibre-composite rotor blades with orange tips for the CoAX 600

mediaSections.title: 160 hp of fuel-injected six-cylinder power
paragraphs: The CoAX 600 uses the ULPower UL390iS, an air-cooled six-cylinder four-stroke engine with 3.9 litres of displacement. It delivers 160 hp at 3,300 rpm and 145 hp continuously, with 370 Nm of torque. That is plenty of reserve for a 600 kg helicopter, with a distinctive sound to match.
Multipoint fuel injection, dual ignition, an integrated 50 A generator and an electric starter keep the engine reliable and easy to operate. It runs on gasoline of at least 98 octane.

images.alt: ULPower UL390iS six-cylinder air-cooled aircraft engine used in the CoAX 600

mediaSections.title: A panoramic view, with or without doors
paragraphs: A large windscreen, lower front windows and full-height door glazing give the crew an unusually wide field of view, with nothing in the way.

The CoAX 600 can also be flown with the doors removed, which gives a completely open side view. That suits aerial photography, filming, survey and observation flights, and on hot days it makes flying feel truly open.

images.alt: CoAX 600 front view in the workshop showing the large bubble windscreen
CoAX 600 two-seat cabin with the door open, showing seats, harnesses and cyclic control

mediaSections.title: A cockpit configured to your mission
paragraphs: Choose anything from a classic round-gauge panel to a full glass cockpit with a large EFIS display. Instruments, avionics and comfort options are specified for each customer, whether for private flying, training or mission work.
For autonomous or optionally piloted conversion, the panel and the electrical system are the integration points for flight-control computers, datalinks and mission sensors.

images.alt: CoAX 600 glass cockpit with EFIS primary flight display and backup gauges
CoAX 600 cockpit with a large multifunction display and twin analogue gauges
CoAX 600 cockpit with a classic round-gauge instrument panel

mediaSections.title: Compact outside, grown-up inside
paragraphs: The CoAX 600 is 7.20 m long overall, 5.61 m along the fuselage, 2.80 m high, with 1.65 m between the skids and a 6.50 m rotor diameter. Its clean, modern shape is small enough for trailers, small helipads and ship decks.

images.alt: CoAX 600 three-view drawing with dimensions: 7,200 mm length, 6,500 mm rotor diameter, 1,650 mm skid width

faq.question: What is the CoAX 600?
faq.answer: The CoAX 600 is a two-seat coaxial ultralight helicopter with a 600 kg maximum take-off weight. It has two counter-rotating rotor planes on one mast and no tail rotor, is powered by a 160 hp ULPower UL390iS engine, and holds a German type certificate issued in June 2023.

faq.question: What is a coaxial helicopter, and why has it no tail rotor?
faq.answer: A coaxial helicopter has two main rotors stacked on the same mast that turn in opposite directions. Their torque cancels out, so no tail rotor is needed to stop the fuselage from spinning. That removes a major hazard and puts all of the engine power into lift.

faq.question: How fast and how high can the CoAX 600 fly?
faq.answer: Maximum cruise speed is 150 km/h (81 kt), never-exceed speed (VNE) is 170 km/h, and the service ceiling is 12,000 ft (about 3,660 m).

faq.question: How much fuel does the CoAX 600 use?
faq.answer: About 19 litres per hour of gasoline (minimum 98 octane), from a 70-litre tank.

faq.question: How much can the CoAX 600 carry?
faq.answer: The minimum empty weight is 340 kg and the maximum take-off weight is 600 kg, which leaves about 260 kg of useful load for crew, fuel and equipment.

faq.question: Is the CoAX 600 certified in Germany?
faq.answer: Yes. The CoAX 600 received its German type certificate as an ultralight (UL) helicopter on 27 June 2023.

faq.question: Can the CoAX 600 be flown without doors?
faq.answer: Yes. It can be operated with the doors removed for a fully open side view, which is popular for aerial photography and observation flights.

faq.question: Can the CoAX 600 be converted to unmanned or autonomous operation?
faq.answer: Yes. With no tail rotor, a compact footprint and about 260 kg of useful load, the CoAX 600 is a suitable base for optionally piloted or autonomous VTOL operation. KUM Services GmbH assesses each mission and engineers the conversion, including flight-control, datalink and sensor integration, on request.

faq.question: How do I get a price or arrange a demonstration?
faq.answer: Send an enquiry through the contact form with "CoAX 600" as your aircraft interest. We reply with the full specification sheet, configuration options and pricing, and arrange a demonstration or a call.

aircrafts.name: CESSNA CITATION 525B
aircrafts.description: The Cessna Citation 525B is a light business jet with twin turbofan power, offering high cruise speed, high-altitude operation, and long range. We convert suitable civil-registered aircraft of this type into high performance autonomous aircraft (HPAA) for rapid coverage and response; airframes can be ferried to the operating location with conversion typically completed on site in a very short period.
details: HPAA integration preserves jet speed, FL450-class ceiling, and transcontinental range within a standard civil-airframe footprint.
Well suited where wide-area transit, time-sensitive repositioning, or high-altitude sensor lines of sight are required for autonomous mission profiles.
Mission equipment and avionics interfaces are engineered to your HPAA payload, certification path, and installation constraints.

aircrafts.name: CESSNA 208
aircrafts.description: The Cessna 208 is a high-wing single turboprop utility aircraft with a strong record in cargo, special mission, and austere-field operations. Selected 208-class airframes are converted into high performance autonomous aircraft (HPAA), using the flexible cabin and cargo door for sensors, mission equipment, and logistics payloads while retaining worldwide parts and maintenance access.
details: HPAA configuration leverages strong short-field and unpaved-surface capability for logistics, surveillance, and multi-role autonomous mission kits.
Turboprop economics and global support networks keep operating cost predictable for sustained HPAA programmes.
Electrical, structural, and datalink interfaces are defined for your HPAA mission computers, sensors, and power budget.

aircrafts.name: C-130J
aircrafts.description: The Lockheed Martin C-130J Super Hercules is a four-engine turboprop tactical transport with very long range and a high-volume cargo hold. Where programme scope allows, integration converts suitable airframes toward high performance autonomous aircraft (HPAA) operation for the largest payloads and mission-system footprints.
details: HPAA-oriented integration uses exceptional range and payload for strategic lift, large sensor suites, or heavy mission equipment in a single airframe.
Rear loading and roll-on/roll-off flexibility support pallets, vehicles, and specialized mission racks for autonomous mission roles.
Planning covers structural interfaces, power and cooling, EMI considerations, and certification-aligned milestones for HPAA systems.

aircrafts.name: Beech King Air 350
aircrafts.description: The Beech King Air 350 is a pressurized twin turboprop with long endurance, stable cruise, and a proven multi-mission record. Civil King Air–class platforms are strong candidates for conversion to high performance autonomous aircraft (HPAA) for ISR, special missions, and related roles, with global support and a mature maintenance ecosystem.
details: HPAA integration remains flexible for sensors, communications, and operational mission kits.
We engineer conversion and integration to match your performance, endurance, and maintenance expectations.
A strong option when you need long endurance and versatility in an HPAA configuration.

aircrafts.name: Pilatus PC-12
aircrafts.description: The Pilatus PC-12 is a versatile single-engine turboprop utility aircraft from Switzerland, known for short-field performance, a pressurized cabin, and multi-role use. Selected PC-12–class civil airframes are converted into high performance autonomous aircraft (HPAA) for executive, cargo, medevac, surveillance, and special-mission roles—combining turboprop efficiency with rugged field capability.
details: Crew and cabin layouts vary; dimensions and weights support HPAA mission planning. Conversion preserves the PC-12’s operational strengths while integrating autonomous mission systems.
Excellent short-runway operation from paved and unpaved strips supports HPAA deployment to austere locations.
Single PT6A-67P power and cabin/cargo flexibility are integrated with your HPAA sensors, datalinks, and mission computers.
